cards.back:
An idea that you can test, giving a reason for what you think will happen.
Example: Our hypothesis is that warmer water dissolves salt faster.
cards.say: hypothesis. An idea that you can test, giving a reason for what you think will happen. Example: Our hypothesis is that warmer water dissolves salt faster.

cards.back:
A scientific test to find an answer.
Example: We carried out an investigation into friction.
cards.say: investigation. A scientific test to find an answer. Example: We carried out an investigation into friction.

cards.back:
The thing you change in a test.
Example: The independent variable is the amount of light.
cards.say: independent variable. The thing you change in a test. Example: The independent variable is the amount of light.

cards.back:
The thing you measure.
Example: The dependent variable is the height of the plant.
cards.say: dependent variable. The thing you measure. Example: The dependent variable is the height of the plant.

cards.back:
A thing you keep the same.
Example: The amount of water is a control variable.
cards.say: control variable. A thing you keep the same. Example: The amount of water is a control variable.

cards.back:
A test where only one thing changes.
Example: Use the same cup every time to keep it a fair test.
cards.say: fair test. A test where only one thing changes. Example: Use the same cup every time to keep it a fair test.

cards.back:
A statement of what you expect to happen.
Example: My prediction is that the ball will roll further on the smooth floor.
cards.say: prediction. A statement of what you expect to happen. Example: My prediction is that the ball will roll further on the smooth floor.

cards.back:
Something you notice with your senses or instruments.
Example: Our observation was that bubbles appeared.
cards.say: observation. Something you notice with your senses or instruments. Example: Our observation was that bubbles appeared.

cards.back:
A value found with an instrument.
Example: The measurement was 24 degrees Celsius.
cards.say: measurement. A value found with an instrument. Example: The measurement was 24 degrees Celsius.

cards.back:
How close a measurement is to the true value.
Example: A digital thermometer gives good accuracy.
cards.say: accuracy. How close a measurement is to the true value. Example: A digital thermometer gives good accuracy.

cards.back:
How much you can trust results because they repeat.
Example: Repeating the test improves reliability.
cards.say: reliability. How much you can trust results because they repeat. Example: Repeating the test improves reliability.

cards.back:
A link between two variables.
Example: There is a correlation between temperature and speed of dissolving.
cards.say: correlation. A link between two variables. Example: There is a correlation between temperature and speed of dissolving.

cards.back:
Information that supports a conclusion.
Example: The graph is evidence for our idea.
cards.say: evidence. Information that supports a conclusion. Example: The graph is evidence for our idea.

cards.back:
To judge how good a test was and how it could be improved.
Example: Evaluate your method and suggest changes.
cards.say: evaluate. To judge how good a test was and how it could be improved. Example: Evaluate your method and suggest changes.

cards.back:
A tool that helps you identify living things by answering questions.
Example: Use the key to name this leaf.
cards.say: key. A tool that helps you identify living things by answering questions. Example: Use the key to name this leaf.

cards.back:
A book or website with information found by other people.
Example: We used a secondary source to find the distance to the Moon.
cards.say: secondary source. A book or website with information found by other people. Example: We used a secondary source to find the distance to the Moon.

cards.back:
A plan that finds hazards and says how to stay safe.
Example: We wrote a risk assessment before using hot water.
cards.say: risk assessment. A plan that finds hazards and says how to stay safe. Example: We wrote a risk assessment before using hot water.

cards.back:
Giving results that are close together when repeated.
Example: The readings were precise, all within one millimetre.
cards.say: precise. Giving results that are close together when repeated. Example: The readings were precise, all within one millimetre.

cards.back:
The gap between values on a scale or between readings.
Example: We took a reading at ten minute intervals.
cards.say: interval. The gap between values on a scale or between readings. Example: We took a reading every ten minutes.
